designSummary: Hybrid implementation-effectiveness study: descriptive implementation outcomes with confidence intervals, a concurrent adjusted comparison of 90-day outcomes, and paired utility change.
sampleSize: About 300 eligible discharges from Hospital A in 12 months give a 95 percent confidence interval of about 5.5 percentage points either side for reach near 60 percent. For 90-day readmission or death near 30 percent, about 300 Hospital A and 400 comparison discharges give about 85 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect a 10-point difference (30 against 20 percent); smaller differences would be estimated imprecisely, which is why no cost-effectiveness claim will be made from this study. About 200 consenting clinic patients with paired questionnaires give a utility change estimate with a 95 percent confidence interval of about 0.03 either side, assuming a standard deviation of change of 0.2.
primaryAnalysis: Reach as a proportion with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval, monthly on a run chart; fidelity likewise.
secondaryAnalysis: Logistic regression of 90-day readmission or death on hospital group, adjusted for age, sex, ejection fraction category, comorbidity score, prior admissions and length of stay; paired utility change with 95 percent confidence interval; cost per episode with bootstrap intervals.
missingData: Missing utilities are described by visit attendance and analysed with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis; missing linked outcomes are not imputed.
multiplicity: One primary implementation outcome; the rest are inputs to a later model and are reported with intervals only.
software: R; the costing spreadsheet is archived with the analysis code.
overfittingGuards: Six adjustment variables fixed in advance
No cost per QALY computed from this study's effectiveness estimate alone
Clinic protocol frozen during the study
summary: Precise reach estimates; readmission comparison powered only for a large difference; utilities and costs collected for a later model.
